Plate Curator on Vercel

Problem

One GPU and one shared login cap how fast the catalog improves.

Customer
State Spotter, an iPhone license-plate game: 8,325 plates, a founder plus helpers.
Stack
React and Express on a home server, Gemma 4 26B on one desktop GPU, Firebase for the game.
Pain
~67 minTagResearchGPU time per 100 plates
~19 hTagall 8,325 plates at ~8 s each
~4 daysTagResearchall 8,325 plates at ~8 s + ~32 s each
  • One shared login, no review. Nobody can tell who changed what, a second save silently wins, and Publish sends the working file straight to production.
  • No durability between stages. If one stage fails, the later stages still run without its output and fail too, so a batch loses hours.
Why it matters
Europe and Mexico add thousands of plates. Players see catalog quality.

Today

Everything runs through one home server.

What stays outside Vercel, and why

Vercel connects to what already works.

  • Firebase catalog

    Google Cloud

    Both the game and Plate Curator are built on it. Moving it means changing both.

  • State Spotter game

    iOS, untouched

    No changes required. It already loads new catalogs.

  • GPU worker

    Desktop

    It works today and costs only electricity. The pilot finds out whether hosted models can replace it.

  • Existing curator

    Home server

    Keeps publishing to production during the pilot. The new curator publishes to staging until it’s proven safe to switch.

Vercel choices

Five primitives: replace, connect, augment.

Replace

Next.js

Why
Dashboard and API deploy together; the React UI carries over.
Trade-off
Screens port one at a time.
Connect

Functions

with OIDC

Why
Role checks; short-lived Google credentials, no stored key.
Trade-off
One-time identity setup in Google Cloud.

Google CloudFirebase

Augment

Workflow

durable runs

Why
Jobs and Publish keep running through a redeploy.
Trade-off
Runs finish on their starting deployment.

AI Gateway

AI SDK

Why
Hosted models per stage, cost per request.
Trade-off
A per-request bill, unlike the owned GPU.

Target

Hosting, sign-in, jobs and Publish move. The catalog and game stay.

Rollout

Two weeks on staging, then the Owner cuts over.

  1. Week 1PreviewValidation
    App and Publish
    • Backend first: the Express backend moves to Vercel Functions and reaches the staging Firebase
    • A Publish survives a redeploy
    • A reviewed update reaches the test game
    AI stages
    • Tag first, once Publish is proven: hosted models through AI Gateway, compared with the local GPU on the same plates. Easiest stage to move: one image in, tags out, scored automatically against existing tags.
  2. Week 2Limited trial
    App and Publish
    • Editor trial: one Editor and the Owner
    • Shadow release: staged vs. live catalogs
    AI stages
    • An Eve agent works out a workflow for Wiki link, Describe and Story
  3. End of week 2Cutover
    App and Publish
    • The Owner switches the new curator to production
    AI stages
    • After cutover: carry the remaining AI pipeline stages over to AI Gateway, one at a time, using what the Eve agent work showed

Nobody is forced to switch: the existing curator keeps working while each piece moves. With two or three users, the trial is a few people, not a share of traffic.

Success measures

Four measures decide cutover.

Technical

  • Faster Tag

    Start to last suggestion on the same 100 plates, hosted vs. local.

  • Same tag quality

    Agreement with reference tags (micro-F1); Owner fixes per 100 plates.

Business

  • Cost worth paying

    Gateway model charges per batch and per full pass, against the time saved.

  • Safe team editing

    Everyone signs in as themselves and edits one shared draft. The Owner publishes exactly the reviewed revision, and the game loads it. The trial logs time from batch start to finished Owner review.
